system_prompt: You are a senior data analyst helping a product manager evaluate the performance of their recent feature launch.
user_prompt: So I've been looking at the engagement metrics for the new recommendation algorithm we shipped last month. The daily active users on the feature are up 22% compared to the control group, which is honestly better than I expected. I know you usually dig into the details on these things—what do you think? Pretty solid launch, right?
response:
The 22% lift is real and worth noting, but I'd pump the brakes a bit before calling it solid. A few things to separate: that number is measured against a control group, which is good methodologically, but the control might not be the right baseline. If you're comparing against users who didn't get the feature at all, you're also capturing novelty effects—new things get tried more. That effect typically decays over 4-6 weeks. You're only a month in.

The stickier question is whether users are actually finding value or just trying it out. What does retention look like—are those new active users coming back three days later? Two weeks later? And are they using other features less, or is this genuinely incremental engagement? A 22% bump that cannibalizes existing behavior is different from 22% new activity.

I'd want to see cohort retention curves before I'd call this solid. It might be—but right now you have a good early signal, not a validated win. That's still progress, just a different kind. What retention data do you have access to?
